stemBlocks.value: In triangle OAB, OA = a and OB = b. The point P divides AB so that AP : PB = 2 : 1. (a) Express the vector AB in terms of a and b. (b) Express the vector AP in terms of a and b. (c) Hence show that OP = (1/3)a + (2/3)b.
Think first: Convert the ratio into a fraction of the whole: AP : PB = 2 : 1 means AP is two-thirds of AB.

solutionSteps.instruction: Write OP as a route through A.

strategyBlocks.value: Write AB as a route through O, take two-thirds of it for AP, then travel O to A to P.

whyThisWorks.value: Any journey between two points can be rerouted through a third, which is why AB becomes AO + OB and turns into b − a. A ratio along a line is a fraction of the whole displacement, so P sits two-thirds of the way from A to B. Notice the coefficients of a and b in the final answer add to 1 — that is the signature of a point lying on the line AB, and a quick way to check this kind of result.

commonErrors.misconception: Writing AB = a − b instead of b − a; the route runs from A, so AO = −a comes first.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Writing AB = a − b instead of b − a; the route runs from A, so AO = −a comes first.

commonErrors.misconception: Taking AP = (1/2)AB by treating the ratio as a fraction directly instead of 2 parts out of 3.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Taking AP = (1/2)AB by treating the ratio as a fraction directly instead of 2 parts out of 3.

commonErrors.misconception: Stopping at OP = a + (2/3)(b − a) without simplifying to the required form.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Stopping at OP = a + (2/3)(b − a) without simplifying to the required form.

examTip.value: Check any 'point on a line' vector answer by adding the coefficients — if they do not total 1, the point is not on that line and you have slipped somewhere.
